purpose: Personal-investment research only. The supplied robotics transcript was used for idea generation; company claims were rechecked against issuer results and regulatory filings.

framework.summary: Adoption is ranked by task structure and customer payback, not by how human-like the machine looks.

waves.name: Structured logistics + fixed industrial automation
waves.why: Controlled environments, repeatable tasks, mature safety practices and measurable labour and throughput ROI.

waves.name: Cobots + mobile manipulation + constrained service robots
waves.why: AI expands task coverage while deployments remain geofenced, supervised and workflow-specific.

waves.name: Industrial humanoids
waves.why: Human-shaped facilities help, but dexterity, reliability, battery life, safety and total cost still need proof.

waves.name: Open-world consumer robots
waves.why: Unstructured environments compound edge cases, liability and price sensitivity.

screenedOut.reason: Commercial deployment is real, but Q1 2026 revenue was only $3.0m against full-year non-GAAP operating-expense guidance of $160m-$170m. Economics do not clear the Power Stack bar.
The pending $5.375bn ABB Robotics acquisition is strategically relevant, but robotics remains too diluted within SoftBank's conglomerate and investment-portfolio risk.
Useful sector benchmark, but outside the preferred listed-market set and too valuation-sensitive for promotion without a longer public reporting record.

notes: Deployment counts alone are not treated as proof of attractive unit economics.
Component and enabling-layer exposure ranks ahead of humanoid-OEM hype when financial evidence is stronger.
